comparator.name: Bèta-gamma
comparator.route: Earth Sciences major with Consultancy for Sustainability as the Year 2 practice project
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–2027 curriculum specifies a common 60-EC first year, two interdisciplinary projects plus 51 EC in the selected major in Year 2, and a final interdisciplinary project plus 54 EC in the selected major in Year 3. The public programme page lists 21 formal majors but does not publish a dependable course-level EC split for each major. For this generic normalized target, Earth Sciences is selected by the neutral first-listed-major tie-break before UCR comparison. Its 105 EC is therefore preserved as two year-level aggregate components. The Year 2 project choice is Consultancy for Sustainability, the first listed option under the same neutral rule. The Year 3 major aggregate includes the bachelor thesis; no separate thesis EC is stated on the cited public curriculum. The selected path is a neutral comparison construct, not an officially privileged route.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the broad programme-defining interests and integrates science, society, humanities, research and communication. The two strongest coherent research-derived directions from the remaining generator interests are AI, Technology & Society and Sustainability, Cities & Public Policy; both pass the evidence, coherence, distinctness and feasibility gates. Cognition, Life, Health & Education and Society, Power, Culture & Resilience are coherent but cannot be added after the maximum of three alternatives is reached. Every schedule contains exactly 24 courses/180 EC, satisfies prerequisite and term constraints, and has substantial advanced-level depth.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce quantitative and qualitative research methods and critical analysis of evidence.
Both introduce programming and computational problem solving; the Amsterdam component also foregrounds AI in society.
Both develop mathematical methods used in scientific and computational analysis.
Both develop applied interdisciplinary sustainability analysis; Amsterdam frames this explicitly as consultancy practice.
Earth Systems Modelling represents a substantive Earth-science component within the much broader 51-EC major aggregate.
No selected UCR course reproduces the integrated nine-EC arc from cosmology through the origins of life.
No selected UCR course reproduces the dedicated interdisciplinary Emergence component.
The 54-EC Year 3 Earth Sciences aggregate, including its thesis, is structurally broader than any single selected UCR course and has no dependable public internal EC split.
Both examine states, institutions and people; UCR approaches them through comparative politics.
Both study social life and institutions in urban settings, with different disciplinary emphases.
No selected UCR course is a dedicated philosophy-of-science component.
Both introduce cognition through brain-and-behaviour perspectives.
No selected UCR course is directly equivalent to Amsterdam’s separately credited first interdisciplinary research project.
No selected UCR course is directly equivalent to the separately credited analysis-of-interdisciplinary-research project.
No selected UCR course is directly equivalent to Amsterdam’s separately credited final interdisciplinary research project.

notes.text: Bèta-gamma prescribes a common interdisciplinary first year and four cross-disciplinary projects before embedding 105 EC in a conventional disciplinary major. UCR instead builds one student-designed 180-EC Liberal Arts and Sciences curriculum from 24 courses, subject to progression and advanced-level requirements.

The official public curriculum gives the selected Earth Sciences major only as 51 EC in Year 2 and 54 EC in Year 3, with the thesis inside the latter total. Those aggregates are preserved rather than inventing course names or a thesis EC value.
The cited Bèta-gamma curriculum is Dutch-taught, whereas the UCR alternatives are English-taught.
